_about: Reusable reasoning frameworks. A kit names one framework and inherits its prompts, feedback templates and default priority-tier explanations; a kit or an issue may override any of them. Feedback templates use <name> placeholders filled by the engine (<name|cap> capitalises).

text.acceptableWhy: Dealing with <other> matters, but dealing with <first> has to come first.
text.redundantWhy: <done|cap>, so that step is not needed and only delays dealing with <first>.
text.redundantClearWhy: <done|cap>, so that step is not needed and only delays work that is ready to go ahead.
text.redundantMis: Repeating a step that is already done is always the careful choice.
text.ignoreWhy: Carrying on as if nothing were wrong leaves <short> unresolved.
text.proceedMis: If the work can technically continue, it should continue.
text.orderMis: Every real issue matters equally, so the order does not matter.
text.planReverseWhy: Both steps are needed, but the order is backwards: dealing with <first> has to come before <other>.
text.planSecondWhy: The first step is right, but the second step mishandles <short>.

tiers.1: Anything that could hurt someone comes before other work.
tiers.2: Work cannot go ahead until it is allowed under the stated rules.
tiers.3: Acting on missing or wrong information wastes everything that follows.
tiers.4: The people affected need to hear about the problem before it grows.
tiers.5: Improvements can wait until the immediate problems are handled.

frameworks.name: Identify the critical information
frameworks.description: The student decides which missing or unclear fact must be obtained before acting, and recognises when the fact is already in hand.

decision: What is the most appropriate action?
What should you do?
nextstep: What is the best next step right now?
plan: Which plan handles this situation best?
order: Put these steps in a sensible order.

frameworks.name: Evaluate competing priorities
frameworks.description: Several demands compete; urgency, importance, dependencies and consequences decide which comes first.

decision: What is the most appropriate action?
How should you handle this?
plan: Which plan handles these demands best?
order: Put these tasks in a sensible order.

frameworks.name: Choose the safest appropriate action
frameworks.description: The student separates safe responses from shortcuts that add risk, and recognises when a hazard is already controlled.

decision: What is the safest appropriate action?
What should you do?
nextstep: What is the safest next step right now?
plan: Which plan handles this situation safely?
order: Put these steps in a safe order.
find: Which line is the safety problem?

frameworks.name: Resolve conflicting instructions
frameworks.description: Instructions disagree; the student works out which conflict matters and who is authorised to settle it.

decision: What is the most appropriate action?
How should you handle these instructions?
nextstep: What is the best next step right now?
plan: Which plan handles these instructions best?
order: Put these steps in a sensible order.

frameworks.name: Identify a communication failure
frameworks.description: The student spots ambiguity, missing context, tone problems, incomplete handoffs or the wrong channel, and repairs them.

decision: What is the most appropriate response?
What should you do?
nextstep: What is the best next step right now?
plan: Which plan fixes the communication best?
order: Put these steps in a sensible order.
find: Which line is the communication problem?

frameworks.name: Evaluate evidence and reliability
frameworks.description: The student separates verified information from assumptions, outdated data and unreliable sources.

decision: What is the most appropriate action?
What should you do with this information?
nextstep: What is the best next step before using this information?
plan: Which plan uses the information most responsibly?
order: Put these steps in a sensible order.

frameworks.name: Identify a process dependency
frameworks.description: The student works out what must happen before another workplace action can proceed.

decision: What is the most appropriate action?
plan: Which plan respects what each step depends on?
order: Put these steps in an order that respects what each one depends on.

frameworks.name: Evaluate a numerical decision
frameworks.description: Calculations, rates, budgets, quantities and measurements decide the answer; the engine calculates it from the generated numbers.

decision: Which choice is correct?
What is the best decision?
find: Which line contains the calculation error?

frameworks.name: Respond to an unexpected change
frameworks.description: Resources, schedules, priorities or requirements change; the student adapts the plan and tells the right people.

decision: What is the most appropriate response to the change?
What should you do?
nextstep: What is the best next step right now?
plan: Which plan adapts to the change best?
order: Put these steps in a sensible order.

frameworks.name: Evaluate an ethical dilemma
frameworks.description: Honesty, confidentiality, fairness, professionalism and accountability pull against convenience or pressure.

decision: What is the most appropriate action?
What should you do?
nextstep: What is the best next step right now?
plan: Which plan handles this situation best?
order: Put these steps in a sensible order.

frameworks.name: Identify a root cause
frameworks.description: The student targets the underlying cause that the evidence points to rather than the visible symptom.

decision: What is the most appropriate action?
What response gets at the real cause?
nextstep: What is the best next step right now?
plan: Which plan deals with the real causes best?
order: Put these steps in a sensible order.

frameworks.name: Evaluate consequences
frameworks.description: Several plausible actions are compared by predicting which best meets the workplace objective under the stated conditions.

decision: Which action best meets the goal?
What is the most appropriate action?
nextstep: What is the best next step right now?
plan: Which plan leads to the best outcome?
order: Put these steps in a sensible order.
